lessons.title: Lesson 1: Brain + Body
lessons.desc: Heads up: this is a replay of the live program, so you’ll hear me mention the group chat. Want the next live round or 1:1? Email savannah@colourmeneurospicy.com.au for a returning-student discount.
prompts: Where have you been neglecting your responsibility to take care of your body?
It’s okay, we’ve all been there. This is about being thankful for your body and brain, then worshipping it by starting to nourish it and take care of it just 1% better tomorrow.
What’s one really small thing you’ll commit to doing every day to look after your brain, body, mind and nervous system?
Keep it tiny, so it’s easy to keep: eating lunch, drinking one bottle of water, regulating your nervous system before bed, a short walk instead of scrolling. One small action, every day.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Conscious + Unconscious Mind
prompts: What’s something you consciously want to do or achieve that you feel your unconscious mind keeps sabotaging? And for what purpose do you feel it’s stopping you? (What’s it trying to protect you from?)
This is going to help you uncover some patterns that will be useful to know for future lessons.
What are some of your unconscious habits you would like to change? (The things you do on autopilot.)
For me, it’s reaching for a sugary snack when I’m bored, or scratching my skin when I’m uncomfortable or concentrating.
Did any of these beliefs ring true for you? What other beliefs have you collected over the years that aren’t serving you? Jot down anything that comes to mind.
For me, in the past they all hit true, and I’m grateful to say I’m overcoming them all using the processes you’re going to learn in this program.
What shitty situation are you staying in just because it’s familiar? (But it’s actually keeping you stuck out of fear of change?)

I’ve stayed in relationships, jobs, careers, houses and bloody cities way too long because it was “known”, and that was easier than leaning into new, uncomfortable situations that could likely lead to a better life.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Nervous System
prompts: Do you believe your vagal tone is high (less reactive to stimulation) or low (more reactive to stimulation)?

Think about the last time you blew up over a lot happening at once. What tipped you over the edge? How much had accumulated? What did you need to do earlier in the day to avoid it? Was it the stacking effect, more than the things themselves?
What bodily messages has your brain been sending you that you may not have realised were a warning sign?

Headaches: thinking too much and not drinking enough water? Aching back: sitting too long, or what are you pushing to the back? Tummy aches: how long have you been stressed and repressing your emotions? That’s all held in the gut.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Neurotransmitters + Hormones
prompts: In what ways has your brain been “sabotaging” you to meet your daily DOSE? And how can you meet those needs more healthily?

Start replacing the negative behaviours with positive ones that move you toward your goals. I replaced doom scrolling with microlearning: books all around the house, so whenever I grabbed my phone looking for a fix, I picked up a book instead. For now, just notice the ones that aren’t serving you.

lessons.title: Activity: Your daily DOSE
lessons.desc: Pick everything you’d love from the DOSE menu, build a quick daily DOSE routine, and get a fun plan whenever you want one.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Anxiety
lessons.desc: Write a list of the situations that make you anxious, then work through each one with the What If Workout.
prompts: What situations tend to give you feelings of anxiousness? Write a list, then use the What If Workout to work through each of them.

lessons.title: Activity: What If Workout
lessons.desc: For when your brain starts spiralling into the future. Get it out of your head and onto the page.
lessons.tip: For when your brain starts spiralling into the future. Get it out of your head and onto the page.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Fight or Flight
lessons.desc: Knowing what your states are, in what situations, and around which people you tend to use each one, is super helpful for changing the way you respond. Sometimes just becoming aware of it is enough.
prompts: Have you been in fight or flight for a while now? Shutdown, burnout? Could the stress you’ve experienced have landed you in a shutdown state so your nervous system can rest?
It’s okay. I’ve been there, and it’s exactly why you’re in this course right now. I’ve got you!
Which state tends to be your default: fight, flight, freeze or fawn? (Defensive, avoidant, shut down or people-pleasing.) In what situations, and around which people?

You can be a range. With my husband I was more defensive because I felt safer to be me. With friends I was more people-pleasing or avoidant, and with strangers I was a freeze operator. Sometimes just becoming aware of it is enough.

lessons.title: Activity: Pause
lessons.desc: Little pockets of slow so your nervous system can catch up. Build your own pause menu.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Body
lessons.desc:
Keys to a happy body: it might not be easy, but it is simple!

🔑 Drink water
🔑 Eat more energy than you burn (and regularly)
🔑 Move your body (we weren’t designed to be stationary beings)
🔑 Rest: your eyes after screens, your brain after thinking hard, your legs after running
🔑 Sleep: a good night-time routine, no screens, read to tire your eyes, empty your mind into a journal

Where have you neglected yourself and your needs, and how can you improve them by just 1% today, and every day?

Your body sends signals. Headaches, an aching back, tummy troubles, tight shoulders, a clenched jaw, a stiff neck, tired eyes, sore feet, aching hands, trouble sleeping, exhaustion: each has a practical side (water, posture, screens, sleep) and a question worth asking (What am I carrying? What am I avoiding? Where do I need more support?).

You don’t have to force a meaning. Sometimes an aching back needs a different chair, and sometimes the question about support opens an important conversation. Both deserve attention.
prompts: Where have you neglected yourself and your needs, and how can you improve them by just 1% today and every day?
What signals has your body been sending you? Does the symbolism help you notice something worth exploring?

Tight shoulders: what are you carrying that isn’t yours to carry? Clenched jaw: what words are you biting back? Sore feet: are you letting yourself move at your own pace? You don’t have to force a meaning. Sometimes an aching back just needs a different chair.
lessons.tip: Keys to a happy body: drink water, eat enough (and regularly), move your body, rest, and sleep. It might not be easy, but it is simple.

lessons.title: Activity: Move
lessons.desc: Why moving matters for stress, and your own move menu at every energy level.

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Neuroplasticity
prompts: What have you installed unconsciously? What unwanted outcome do you keep experiencing that you’d like to change?
Mine were doomscrolling, the chocolate thing, putting others before myself constantly, avoiding exercise… and I’m actively rewiring those paths all the time.

lessons.title: Lesson 9: Breathing
lessons.desc:
Minimum once a day, ideally two or three times.

This is the main key to building a resilient nervous system! Only 5 to 15 minutes a day, and you’ll strengthen that spindly tree into a stable, reliable one.
lessons.tip: Minimum once a day, ideally 2–3 times. Only 5–15 minutes a day, and you’ll strengthen that spindly tree into a stable, reliable one.

lessons.title: Activity: Breathwork
lessons.desc: Your two go-to breaths (the 5-minute daily breath and the physiological sigh), a guided breathing tool with soothing sounds, and what to do for the state you’re in.

lessons.title: Embodiment: Vagal Tone Workout
lessons.desc:
Small daily practices to support regulation, recovery and resilience.

Everything in this program is designed to build a more resilient nervous system. Like building a muscle, small repetitions add up.

Your four daily practices (write them on a sticky note for your mirror or computer):
1. DOSE: get your daily dose of dopamine, oxytocin, serotonin and endorphins.
2. BREATHE: your five-minute breathing practice, at least once a day.
3. PAUSE: little pauses through the day.
4. MOVE: get your body moving.

Missed one? Pick it up at the next opportunity. No catching up required. It’s about the 1% actions.

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.desc:
This video will probably feel overwhelming, and because you’re AuDHD, you want to know why you’re learning everything before I actually teach you the thing… I see you, because I am you!

You’re probably thinking, I didn’t sign up for this. Chill, it’s exactly what you didn’t know you needed. Trust me. It will all make sense soon.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Your Experience of the World
prompts: What does your current experience of the world look like?
Family, friends, upbringing (childhood), genetics, environment, choices and desires. Make a heading for each and jot down a few things that come to mind.
How do you feel about your experience of the world?

Are you grateful for the life you’ve lived so far? Sad? Wish it were different? A bit of both? It’s okay if you’re not there yet. By the end of the program you may feel differently about the cards you’ve been dealt.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Your Memories + RAS Filter
lessons.desc:
⭐️ PAUSE activity: add PAUSE to your DOSE and Breathe sticky notes.

A reminder to take a five-minute pause, or even a few physiological breaths, throughout the day. Stop rushing everything and everywhere, and give all that information your brain is processing a second to catch up.
prompts: Your truth, my truth, not THE truth. Where in life has that been true for you?

Have there been moments where you remembered an event differently from someone else, and you each thought the other was lying? What if two things could be true at once, and the bits your brain saved as “important” were just different to theirs?
Can you recall more “negative” memories than positive ones?
The heavier emotions like anger, fear and sadness feel more important to our survival than joy or love, so the brain saves them to protect us, and then ends up looking for more of them.

lessons.title: Side Quest: Synaptic Pruning (our super computer brain)
prompts: What information has your brain kept? And what synapses did it prune?

Remember how, if you don’t ride a bike for a few years, it only takes a few minutes to feel confident again? Your brain re-opened a weaker pathway and strengthened it back up now it knows you need it.

lessons.title: Side Quest: Overstimulation (introducing the energy audit)
lessons.desc: You’ll find the energy audit in the Energy Audit lesson later this week.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Proof Portfolio
lessons.desc:
Your RAS filter is what you use to collect “proof”, and you can train it to see the positive instead of the negative. For now, start noticing when you’re seeing the negative frame, and how you could see the positive intention instead.

⭐️ Start a journal of daily wins: something you enjoyed, something beautiful you saw, something you’re grateful for. Watch how much more of the good stuff you begin to notice.
prompts: Are you a glass-half-full or glass-half-empty person naturally? (Be honest with yourself)

Example: “That day was shit, EVERYTHING went wrong. I spilled my coffee, my boss was rude, I got a parking ticket”, completely forgetting you finished a big project, got a free gift voucher, and your partner made a beautiful dinner.

lessons.title: Activity: Start your proof portfolio
lessons.desc: Add your first piece of proof, then have a look around the proof part of your Becoming Book.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Beliefs
lessons.desc:
❤️ Before you begin: your wellbeing comes first.

These questions may bring up difficult memories or emotions. You don’t need to revisit, describe or share traumatic experiences to benefit from this. Keep things at a level that feels manageable, skip any question, or stop altogether. There’s nothing to prove by pushing through distress.

This program offers education, coaching and self-reflection. It is not therapy, trauma treatment or a substitute for personalised mental health care.

If you feel overwhelmed, disconnected or unsafe, pause. Look around, notice your surroundings, feel your feet on the floor, and reach out to someone you trust.

If you have thoughts of self-harm or suicide, stop and get support straight away. In Australia, call Lifeline on 13 11 14 (24/7) or text 0477 13 11 14. If you’re in immediate danger, call 000. Outside Australia, contact your local crisis line or emergency number. Program messages are not a crisis service, so please don’t wait for a reply from me to get help.
prompts: Childhood conditioning: what sort of behaviour was or wasn’t modelled to you growing up?
Money, confidence, self-worth, love, communication, values, behaviour. What do you catch yourself thinking or doing and wonder why? Likely you picked it up from what was modelled to you.
Reflect on the significant people you looked up to or grew up around. What behaviours did they pass to you? What was their upbringing like?
This isn’t about blame. They likely did the best they could with the resources they had. Just notice, note it down and leave it be for now.
What limiting beliefs have you collected over your life from past “trauma”, negative memories or labels given to you?

Go gentle here. You don’t need to go to the depths of anything that doesn’t feel safe. Examples: “I’m not a confident person.” “Travelling isn’t safe.” “I’m socially awkward because I’m autistic.” “I’m ADHD, so I can’t focus.” Each of these is a choice of belief, and there are empowering ones you can hold instead.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Thoughts + Feelings + Actions = Reality
lessons.desc: Map this across every area of your life: business or career, relationships, health, wealth, self-care. All of it.
prompts: What do you not like about your reality right now? (Make a big list)
Example: I hate all the blackheads I have.
What am I currently doing (thoughts, feelings, actions) that is contributing to the reality I don’t want?
Example: I’m not putting effort into my skincare routine. I’d need to wash my face twice a day.
What small action can I take toward the reality I want that feels manageable right now?
Example: wash my face once a day to start.

lessons.desc:
Week 1: track your energy and activities for one week, so you collect data and spot patterns.

Week 2: look at the patterns, find your likely energy lows and highs, and plan your week to support more sustained energy.

Change your state, change your life. To feel joy, put yourself in the state of joy. To break an overthinking loop, change your state. If you take one thing from this course, make it this: practise changing your state.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Model of the World
lessons.desc: Try stepping into the shoes of your mum, dad, siblings, partner, friends, colleagues, even people you have big negative feelings about (these work even better).
prompts: Step into your nearest and dearest’s model of the world. Imagine living their life, having their past, their upbringing, their realities. What do you notice? What do you feel?
Try it for your mum, dad, siblings, partner, friends, colleagues, even people you have big negative associations with (these work even better).

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Perspectives
prompts: Where are your fixed perspectives holding you back from seeing other people’s points of view, or even giving yourself a more expansive point of view?
Where have you made judgements or assumptions about yourself or others without stepping into their shoes?

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Resources + Behaviour
lessons.desc: You can use this for everyday things too: a friend not messaging back, someone forgetting your birthday, a stranger cutting you off in traffic. Seeing that they might not have had the resources to handle it better lets you release the emotion and move on.
prompts: What resources did the people who “hurt” you (or a past version of yourself) need that they didn’t have at the time?

What “bad” behaviour do you hold shame, guilt, anger, resentment or sadness about, that you or someone around you displayed? Can you see the behaviour as bad, and still hold forgiveness toward them as a person?

You don’t have to share that forgiveness with them. Use this for small things too, like a friend not messaging back or someone cutting you off in traffic, so it doesn’t affect your mood for the rest of the day, or your life.
What resources do you need now to change the trajectory of your life moving forward?

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Triggers
lessons.desc: Next time you’re emotionally triggered by what someone says or does, notice: it says more about the bullets in your gun than about the person delivering them.
prompts: What bullets are in your gun?
Next time you’re emotionally triggered by what someone says or does, notice it. It says more about the bullets in your gun than the person delivering it.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Perception is Projection
lessons.desc: This might take some time to land. If you felt neutral about something, your RAS filter wouldn’t have saved it as important. So whatever annoys you is showing you a mirror worth cleaning up.
prompts: What is currently in your reality that annoys you? What do you wish wasn’t being reflected to you right now?

Friend being needy? Ask: where in my life am I being needy, or overextending myself? Judging someone filming content in public? Ask: where am I afraid of being seen? If you felt neutral, your brain wouldn’t have flagged it. It’s a mirror for you to clean up.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Cause and Effect
prompts: Where are you letting the past hold you back from creating the future you desire?
The things that have happened to you, the fears you have, the patterns you have repeated.

lessons.title: Activity: The Understanding Bridge
lessons.desc: A bridge between your perspective, their perspective, and a new understanding that lets you move forward.
lessons.tip: A bridge between your perspective, their perspective, and a new understanding that lets you move forward.

lessons.title: Activity: Pause and Rewind
lessons.desc: Reach for REWIND when you realise you reacted in a way you wish you could take back or do differently next time. Maybe you got defensive, reacted overly emotionally, or it happened so fast on autopilot you barely noticed.
lessons.tip: Reach for Rewind when you’ve reacted in a way you wish you could take back or do differently next time.

lessons.title: Bonus: Nervous System Regulation (RSD edition)
lessons.desc:
My reset steps for RSD or big-emotion moments. You don’t need a fancy device.

1. Breathe 5 seconds in, 5 seconds out. Slow belly breathing, reminding your body “hey babe, we’re safe”.
2. Sway and check in with your body. Jaw tight? Shoulders up? Consciously relax them.
3. Hand flapping. Stimming releases energy instead of bottling it up.
4. Left and right arm tapping.
5. Ground yourself: lie down and let your body feel supported.
6. Weight on your chest: a weighted blanket (or a pet!). Deep pressure helps your body feel safe.
7. Gratitude and reality checking: I am here. I am safe. I am in control of what I do next.
8. Reconnect with your purpose.
9. Somatic dancing to move leftover emotion out of your body.
10. More swaying and movement.

Music matters too. Find songs that remind you who you are. Take what works, leave what doesn’t.
lessons.tip: Breathe 5 in, 5 out. Sway and soften your jaw and shoulders. Stim, tap left and right, ground, add weight on your chest, reality-check, reconnect with your purpose and move it out. Take what works, leave what doesn’t.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Association vs Disassociation
lessons.desc: If you’re in your head, you’re dead!
prompts: Where in your life have you been, or are you, disassociating?
When are you disconnecting from the reality around you and living in your head, in your thoughts?

lessons.title: Activity: Coming Home (into your body)
lessons.desc:
For when you’re stuck in your head, overthinking, ruminating, or halfway down the dark doom hole, and you want to come back to the land of the living. Including what to do in a meltdown or a fight-or-flight amygdala hijack.

This is an experiment, not homework. Try things, keep what feels good, ditch what doesn’t.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Emotions
lessons.desc: The other end of the spectrum: we also suppress excitement, happiness and joy out of fear of being too much, too loud or too dramatic. We’re taught to stay small.
prompts: What moments in your life did you suppress an emotion because it wasn’t okay to express it out loud?
Anger, sadness, fear, hurt, guilt, shame and grief are the big 7 we tend to suppress.

lessons.title: Activity: What am I feeling?
lessons.desc: Do this one before Lesson 4.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Meltdowns
prompts: What are the key signs you’re weeks, days, hours or minutes away from a meltdown?
Becoming aware helps you, and the people who love you, release the emotions before the unplanned, potentially messy explosion.
What do you need to be doing regularly to avoid meltdowns?
